{{short description|American jail facility}}
{{Use American English|date=August 2025}}
'''Alexandria City Jail''' (formally  '''William G. Truesdale - Alexandria Adult Detention Center''') is a jail facility at 2001 Mill Road, [[Alexandria, Virginia]], serving several courts and police agencies in [[Northern Virginia]], including the [[U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia]], commonly called the Alexandria [[United States district court|federal court]].

This facility is not owned or operated by the [[Federal Bureau of Prisons]] (BOP); the facility has an agreement with the [[U.S. Marshals Service]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.alexandriava.gov/sheriff/info/default.aspx?id=8460|title=Detention Center Bureau|publisher=City of Alexandria|accessdate=2020-08-06}}</ref>

==Notable prisoners==
Defendants involved in federal criminal proceedings there are often housed in the jail, including (with approximate dates of incarceration):
* [[Wilbert Lee Evans]] (January 1981), Virginia death row inmate who was convicted of murdering a deputy sheriff while trying to escape the jail<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |date=1981-01-28 |title=Alexandria Deputy Dies After Shooting |pages=1 |work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/richmond-times-dispatch-alexandria-deput/124565506/ |url-status=live |access-date=2023-05-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230513150207/https://www.newspapers.com/article/richmond-times-dispatch-alexandria-deput/124565506/ |archive-date=2023-05-13 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>
* [[Lyndon LaRouche]]<ref name="Weiner" /> (October 1986 – December 1986),<ref name="Weiner" /> Presidential candidate, served 6 years of a 15-year sentence for fraud
* [[Aldrich Ames]]<ref name="Weiner"/> (February 1994 – April 1994), [[CIA]] officer sentenced to life for espionage
* [[William Aramony]]<ref name="Weiner"/> (March 1995 – April 1995), [[United Way of America]] [[CEO]], served 6 years of a 7-year sentence for fraud
* [[Harold James Nicholson]]<ref name="Weiner"/> (November 1996), CIA officer twice convicted of espionage, sentenced to total of 33{{frac|1|2}} years
* [[Robert Hanssen]] (February 2001 – May 2002), [[FBI]] agent serving 15 consecutive life sentences for espionage 
* [[Zacarias Moussaoui]]<ref name="Weiner"/> (December 2001 – May 2006), French citizen, "[[20th hijacker]]" of [[9/11]] plot
* [[John Walker Lindh]] (June 2002 – August 2002), "[[American Taliban]]"
* [[John Allen Muhammad]]  (2002 – 2009), "[[Beltway sniper]]"
* [[John Lee Malvo]] (November 2002), "[[Beltway sniper]]"
* [[Virginia jihad network|Seifullah Chapman]] (2003 – 2004), [[U.S. Marine]] sentenced to 65 years in "[[Virginia jihad network|Virginia Jihad]]" case,<ref>James Dao (March 2, 2004), [https://www.nytimes.com/2004/03/02/us/closing-remarks-in-terror-trial-touch-on-paintball-and-pakistan.html "Closing Remarks in Terror Trial Touch on Paintball and Pakistan"], ''The New York Times''</ref> exonerated in 2018<ref>Bill Chappell (July 20, 2018), [https://www.npr.org/2018/07/20/630766166/judge-vacates-terrorism-convictions-of-man-who-had-trained-with-paintball-group "Judge Vacates Terrorism Convictions Of Man Who Had Trained With Paintball Group"], National Public Radio</ref> 
* [[Iyman Faris]], a.k.a. Mohammad Rauf (April 2003 – October 2003), [[Ohio]] truck driver sentenced to 20 years for plotting to destroy the [[Brooklyn Bridge]] with a [[blowtorch]]<ref>Eric Lichtblau (Oct. 29, 2003), [https://www.nytimes.com/2003/10/29/us/trucker-sentenced-to-20-years-in-plot-against-brooklyn-bridge.html "Trucker Sentenced to 20 Years in Plot Against Brooklyn Bridge"], ''The New York Times''</ref> 
* Dr. [[Ali al-Timimi]] (April 2005 – July 2005), biologist convicted in "[[Virginia jihad network|Virginia Jihad]]" case
* [[Judith Miller (journalist)|Judith Miller]] (July 7, 2005 – September 29, 2005), N.Y. Times reporter jailed for refusing to name her source in [[Plame affair criminal investigation]]
* [[Ahmed Omar Abu Ali]] (February 2005 – March 2006), [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]] national sentenced to 30 years for plotting to assassinate [[George W. Bush]]
* [[Glenn Duffie Shriver]] (2012),<ref name=WiseWash>{{cite web|last=Wise|first=David|url=https://washingtonian.com/2012/06/07/chinas-mole-in-training/|title=Mole-in-Training: How China Tried to Infiltrate the CIA|work=[[Washingtonian (magazine)|Washingtonian]]|date=2012-06-07|access-date=2016-08-06|quote=A week later, Shriver was wearing a green jumpsuit in a cell at the red-brick Alexandria city jail[...]}}</ref> American citizen convicted of offenses related in an attempt to be employed by the CIA to send information to the Chinese government
* [[Eric Harroun]] (March 2013 – September 2013), US citizen who fought for the [[Free Syrian Army]] and was allegedly compelled to fight for the [[al-Qaeda]] offshoot [[al-Nusra Front]]. After it became clear he wasn't fighting for a group classified as terrorist, he was released on minor charges.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Pelton |first=Robert Young |date=11 April 2014 |title=The All-American Life and Death of Eric Harroun |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/the-all-american-life-and-death-of-eric-harroun/ |access-date=2023-04-04 |website=Vice.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="newyorker">{{cite magazine |date=16 February 2015 |title=Lost In Syria |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2015/02/16/lost-syria |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |accessdate=27 May 2015}}</ref><ref name="blogs.phoenixnewtimes.com">{{cite web |last=Hendley |first=Matthew |date=2013-09-20 |title=Eric Harroun, Phoenix Vet Who Fought Syrian Regime, Suddenly Gets a Sweet Plea Deal |url=http://blogs.phoenixnewtimes.com/valleyfever/2013/09/eric_harroun_phoenix_vet_who_f_1.php |accessdate=2013-11-23 |publisher=Blogs.phoenixnewtimes.com |archive-date=2013-10-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131015042058/http://blogs.phoenixnewtimes.com/valleyfever/2013/09/eric_harroun_phoenix_vet_who_f_1.php |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* [[Guccifer|Marcel Lazăr Lehel]] (May 2016 – September 2016), Romanian national sentenced to 52 months for hacking
* [[Paul Manafort]] (July 2018 – )<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://washingtonian.com/2018/08/22/paul-manafort-is-still-in-the-alexandria-jail-what-happens-next/ |title=Paul Manafort is Still in the Alexandria Jail. What Happens Next? |author=Amanda Whiting |date=2018-08-22 |journal=[[Washingtonian (magazine)|Washingtonian]] |access-date=2018-09-01}}</ref><ref name="Weiner">Rachel Weiner (July 12, 2018), [https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/nationworld/ct-paul-manafort-jail-20180712-story.html "Paul Manafort moves to Alexandria jail, a past home to spies and terrorists"], ''Chicago Tribune''</ref>
* [[Maria Butina]] (August 2018 – )<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/alleged-russian-agent-marina-butina-moved-to-virginia-jail-unclear-why |title=Alleged Russian Agent Marina Butina Moved to Virginia Jail, Unclear Why |author=Betsy Woodruff, Pervaiz Shallwani |date=2018-08-18 |publisher=[[The Daily Beast]] |accessdate=2018-09-01}}</ref>
* [[Chelsea Manning]] (March 2019 – 9 May 2019, 16 May 2019 – 12 March 2020)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/public-safety/chelsea-manning-sent-to-jail-for-refusing-to-testify-in-wikileaks-case/2019/03/08/ecb9eda8-41b4-11e9-9361-301ffb5bd5e6_story.html |title=Chelsea Manning sent to jail for refusing to testify in WikiLeaks case |author= Rachel Weiner, Ellen Nakashima |date=2019-03-08 |work=[[The Washington Post]] |accessdate=2019-03-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/05/09/politics/chelsea-manning-release/index.html|title=Chelsea Manning released from Virginia jail after 62 days|website=CNN|access-date=2019-05-10}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/public-safety/chelsea-manning-ordered-released-from-jail/2020/03/12/0ee56efc-6478-11ea-845d-e35b0234b136_story.html |title=Chelsea Manning is released from jail |author= Rachel Weiner |date=2020-03-13 |work=[[The Washington Post]] |accessdate=2020-03-13}}</ref> American activist and [[whistleblower]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pinknews.co.uk/2018/01/15/transgender-activist-chelsea-mannings-senate-video-listed-as-inappropriate-by-youtube/|title=Transgender activist Chelsea Manning's Senate video listed as 'inappropriate' by YouTube - PinkNews · PinkNews|website=www.pinknews.co.uk|access-date=2019-05-10}}</ref> in addition to being a former U.S. Army Soldier
* [[Jake Angeli]], a.k.a. [[Jake Angeli|Jacob Chansley]] (February 2021 – July 2021), "QAnon shaman" American conspiracy theorist who participated heavily in the [[2021 United States Capitol attack]]<ref>Jane Recker (Feb. 4, 2021), [https://washingtonian.com/2021/02/04/the-qanon-shaman-has-been-moved-to-the-alexandria-jail-so-he-can-eat-organic/ "The 'QAnon Shaman' Has Been Moved to the Alexandria Jail So He Can Eat Organic"], ''Washingtonian'' magazine</ref><ref>Yaron Steinbuch (Feb. 5, 2021), [https://nypost.com/2021/02/05/qanon-shaman-unrecognizable-in-mugshot-from-virginia-jail/  "'QAnon Shaman' unrecognizable in mugshot from Virginia jail"], ''New York Post'' </ref><ref>(Feb. 5, 2021), [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/man-who-wore-horns-capitol-riot-moved-virginia-jail-serves-n1256836 "Man who wore horns in Capitol riot moved to Virginia jail that serves organic food"], NBC News via Associated Press </ref><ref>(July 8, 2021), 
[https://www.cbsnews.com/colorado/news/qanon-shaman-colorado-federal-detention-center-jake-angeli-capitol-riot/ "QAnon Shaman, Who Faces Capitol Riot Charges, Being Housed In Denver-Area Detention Center"], CBS News </ref> 
* [[Allison Fluke-Ekren]] (sentenced to 20 years, 2022), American female [[jihadist]]<ref>{{cite web | title=Kansas mom gets 20 years for leading Islamic State battalion|first=Matthew|last=Barakat | publisher=Associated Press| date=1 November 2022 | url=https://apnews.com/article/kansas-7322a6b74bdbe309e972b2562c607b69}}</ref>
